diagnosis: The float32 mismatches are all one-ULP differences between numpy's arcsin and ONNX Runtime's arcsin (e.g. 0.5 -> 0.5235988 vs 0.52359873). The document specifies the result as round(arcsin(X[i])) with roundTiesToEven, but the exact arcsine of 0.5 is irrational, so the correctly-rounded result is not determined by the document alone; the profile leaves accuracy to the accuracy guidelines, and the case module compares bit-for-bit against ORT. The case module's own sweep_spec_examples also fails because it wrote the documented value as np.float32(np.pi/6) rather than the correctly-rounded float32 of pi/6, which is the ORT value. The real-section failures are the case module passing Fraction/Decimal objects to a numpy ufunc, which the document's 'real' section does not require the implementation to accept as a concrete representation.
instruction: Fix the case module: (1) in cases() and sweep_float_domain, do not require bit-for-bit equality with ORT for in-domain float operands; compare with a tolerance of 1 ULP (or compare against a correctly-rounded reference computed in higher precision), since the document specifies round(arcsin(x)) and the exact arcsine is irrational. (2) In sweep_spec_examples, replace np.float32(np.pi/6) with the correctly-rounded float32 value of pi/6 (0.52359873...), i.e. compute the expected value in float64 and round to float32, so the documented example matches the document's own rounding rule. (3) In sweep_real_section, do not pass Fraction/Decimal arrays to impl.asin; the document's 'real' section does not specify a concrete representation, so either skip the real-section sweep or convert to float64 before calling the implementation and compare against the high-precision reference with a tolerance.
